ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$ and intersects $AB$ at point $D$, $DE\parallel BC$, and intersects $AC$ at point $E$. If $BC=9$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In the right-angled triangle $ABC$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore AC= \frac{1}{2}BC= \frac{9}{2}$, \\
$\angle ACB=90^\circ-\angle B=60^\circ$, \\
$\because CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$, \\
$\therefore \angle ACD= \frac{1}{2}\angle ACB=30^\circ$, \\
$\because DE\parallel BC$, \\
$\therefore \angle EDC=\angle DCB=\angle ACD=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore CE=DE$, \\
$\therefore \angle ADC=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ADE=\angle ADC-\angle EDC=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore AE=\frac{1}{2}DE=\frac{1}{2}EC$, \\
$\therefore AE= \frac{1}{3}AC= \frac{1}{3}\times \frac{9}{2}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$
